question: How many cases were administered in fiscal 2026, and how does that compare with the previous two years?
expected_answer: 363 cases (a record), up from 347 in fiscal 2025 and 341 in fiscal 2024 (ICSID).

gold.evidence_quote: The Centre administered 363 cases — the highest in its history — up from 347 in fiscal 2025 and 341 in fiscal 2024.

top3.source: starter/data/The World Bank Group Annual Report 2026.pdf
top3.heading: FIGURE 5: ICSID ADMINISTERED CASES BY FISCAL YEAR
top3.text:
FIGURE 5: ICSID ADMINISTERED CASES BY FISCAL YEAR
Fiscal 2026 was a record year for ICSID. The Centre administered 363 cases — the highest in its history — up from 347 in fiscal 2025 and 341 in fiscal 2024. In addition, ICSID provided services in 15 cases governed by non-ICSID rules in fiscal 2026, 12 of which were conducted under the UNCITRAL rules.

top3.source: starter/data/The World Bank Group Annual Report 2026.pdf
top3.heading: FIGURE 5: ICSID ADMINISTERED CASES BY FISCAL YEAR
top3.text: During fiscal 2026, ICSID registered 60 new cases — 57 arbitrations under the ICSID Convention and three under the Additional Facility Rules — bringing the cumulative total to 1,118 registered cases as of June 30, 2026. On the mediation front, ICSID had received a total of seven requests under Mediation Rule 6 and Mediation Rule 5, with one proceeding administered as of fiscal 2026. The year also saw 83 proceedings concluded, marking the third consecutive fiscal year in which conclusions surpassed 80.

Parties and tribunals chose from in-person, virtual, or hybrid formats based on the needs of each case, with 75 percent of hearings and sessions incorporating remote features supported by ICSID’s audio and video conferencing facilities. Of all the in-person hearings in fiscal 2026, 44 percent were held at ICSID’s hearing center in Washington, D.C., with the remainder taking place at venues agreed upon by the parties: Paris (30 percent), London (12 percent), Singapore (5 percent), and other locations (9 percent).
ICSID continued to see a diverse pool of arbitrators, conciliators, and committee members in fiscal 2026.

question: What share of MIGA's outstanding gross guarantee portfolio was reinsured as of June 30, 2026?
expected_answer: $28.7 billion, or 69 percent, up from 68 percent the previous fiscal year.

gold.evidence_quote: As of June 30, 2026, $28.7 billion or 69 percent of the outstanding gross portfolio was reinsured, up from 68 percent last fiscal year.

top3.source: starter/data/The World Bank Group Annual Report 2026.pdf
top3.heading: FIGURE 3: GROSS GUARANTEE PORTFOLIO EXPOSURE, FISCAL 2022–26 BILLIONS OF DOLLARS REINSURANCE
top3.text:
MIGA ceded $7.5 billion of new business to the reinsurance market during fiscal 2026. MIGA’s objective in using reinsurance is to support its growth while managing portfolio concentration and ensuring efficient capital utilization. The increased use of reinsurance is also in line with the World Bank Group goal of leveraging the private sector into financing development, as well as with MIGA’s strategy of preserving capital to fund future growth, primarily in priority areas. As of June 30, 2026, $28.7 billion or 69 percent of the outstanding gross portfolio was reinsured, up from 68 percent last fiscal year.

Since 1997, MIGA has successfully used reinsurance to leverage its investment guarantee capacity, manage its portfolio risk profile, and foster the growth of the private political risk insurance market. Significant benefits have accrued both to MIGA’s investors, who have gained access to higher levels of coverage for projects in developing countries, and to host countries, which have benefited from much higher levels of productive foreign investment.

top3.text:

Due to record new business volume, as of June 30, 2026, MIGA’s gross outstanding guarantee portfolio reached a record high of $41.4 billion, representing a 13 percent increase. The net outstanding guarantee portfolio increased by 8 percent to a record high of $12.1 billion.

question: How many fraud and corruption cases involving staff and corporate vendors were investigated by the Integrity Vice Presidency, and how many were substantiated?

gold.evidence_quote: INT investigated 54 cases of alleged fraud and corruption involving World Bank staff and corporate vendors and substantiated four cases.

top3.source: starter/data/The World Bank Group Annual Report 2026.pdf
top3.heading: SANCTIONS SYSTEM
top3.text:
The World Bank Group recognized 35 cross-debarments from other multilateral development banks, and 14 World Bank Group entities and individuals were eligible for recognition by other multilateral development banks.
INT investigated 54 cases of alleged fraud and corruption involving World Bank staff and corporate vendors and substantiated four cases.
For more information about the Sanctions System and its annual report, visit www. worldbank.org/integrity. To report suspected fraud or corruption in World Bank Group– financed projects, or by World Bank Group staff and corporate vendors, visit www.worldbank. org/fraudandcorruption.

top3.source: starter/data/The World Bank Group Annual Report 2026.pdf
top3.heading: SANCTIONS SYSTEM
top3.text:
SANCTIONS SYSTEM
The World Bank Group’s Sanctions System addresses allegations of fraud, corruption, collusion, coercion, and obstruction — collectively known as sanctionable practices — in our operations.
In fiscal 2026, following the conclusion of the Integrity Vice Presidency unit’s (INT) investigations, the World Bank Group sanctioned 16 entities and individuals via uncontested determinations of the Chief Suspension and Debarment Officer, three entities and individuals via decisions of the Sanctions Board, and eight entities and individuals via settlement agreements. Twenty entities and individuals met their conditions for release from World Bank Group sanctions.

top3.source: starter/data/The World Bank Group Annual Report 2026.pdf
top3.heading: ETHICS AND INTERNAL JUSTICE SERVICES
top3.text:
In fiscal 2026, EIJ launched a policy on protection against retaliation to strengthen safeguards for staff engaging in protected activities. During the same year, 3,900 staff used EIJ’s services, 9,363 staff received in-person ethics-related training, and 20,447 staff took the online “Delivering with Decency” compliance course.
For more information about Ethics and Internal Justice Services, visit https://www.worldbank. org/en/about/unit/ethics-and-internal-justice-services.
